issues.on_page: Charges for services 4,301 = Cemetery 950 + Pool 3,351 (p12, General Fund departments)
issues.issue: [fixed 2026-10-29: split (split_from p5 line, p12 breakdown) into Recreation Fees 3,351 and Cemetery Fees 950] The report prints the breakdown of this line: pool fees 3,351 (78%) and cemetery fees 950. Under the user rules (2026-10-28) Recreation Fees and Cemetery Fees are their own receipt categories out of charges for services. It should be split (split_from, p12) into Recreation Fees 3,351 and Cemetery Fees 950, or at least take the dominant Recreation Fees with a review note.

[fixed 2026-10-29: category set to Cemetery Fees] Cemetery department charges belong in category Cemetery Fees (detail_category already 'cemetery fees'). scripts/user_rules.py matches on the label only, so it won't fix this.

[fixed 2026-10-29: category set to Recreation Fees] Pool department charges belong in category Recreation Fees (detail_category already 'recreation/pool/park fees'). The label-only rule script won't catch it.

p2 shows 112,371 as operating grants for general government and 19,439 as capital grants (park). The grantor isn't stated, so some of it may be government grants (state aid/federal) and not private donations.

Public works includes the cemetery 7,924, which the detail records as health/welfare. The dominant streets category is defensible, but the statement line and the detail treat the cemetery differently.
Assumed to be the highway allocation; the report doesn't say.

[fixed 2026-10-29: relabelled 'Capital Outlay: Streets/Highways', printed text in printed_label] Capital outlay lines in category capital outlay should be labelled 'Capital Outlay: <function>' (here 'Capital Outlay: Streets/Highways'), with the printed text in printed_label, as was done for the Library and Park lines.
